contributions.detail: THE DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION, flagged loudly. Schedule A (p2) carries exactly ONE entry — a 283.98 personal loan from the candidate to his own campaign — and both of that schedule's printed footers state 283.98. The Summary Page, however, prints Box B (this period) as an oval ZERO and puts the 283.98 in Box C (year to date) with the handwritten annotation '(personal loan to campaign)'. So the one row sums to 283.98 exactly = Box C = both Schedule A footers, and equals NOTHING on the per-period side. Per §A6 that is `cumulative-exact`, not a delta: the filer's arithmetic on the schedule is fine, the figure the rows reconcile to is simply a different SCOPE from the per-period cell this module promotes, so `reconciles_contributions` should stay BLANK = UNKNOWN downstream rather than True. Note the further oddity, transcribed and NOT adjudicated: this is the cycle's FIRST report (Seven days preceding Convention, 04/03/2022), so period and year-to-date cover the same span, and the filer's own ladder does not close either way — A 0 + B 0 = F 0, then F - D would be -283.98 while the close box holds a heavily struck-out figure followed by a hand-drawn oval 0. NOTHING was nudged and no cover was differenced against another. THE LOAN WAS CLASSIFIED BY THE LADDER, NOT BY THE WORD (§B3): Schedule A is where the filer itemized it and Schedule A's own two footers count it, so it is published as the one contribution row this document reports.

expenditures.detail: 3 Schedule B rows on p3: 38.98 + 89.96 + 155.04 = 283.98 EXACTLY = the printed page subtotal = the printed total = the promoted per-period Box D. Box E year-to-date prints the same 283.98 (first report of the cycle). The closure is also what settles row 1's last digit: 283.98 - 89.96 - 155.04 = 38.98 uniquely, and that cell's final digit is written over another glyph (see escalation_note). Arithmetic closure outranks glyph reading.

in_kind_convention: not applicable — the `v. 4.20`-family blank used here carries no in-kind column and no in-kind checkbox, and no row on either schedule is annotated in-kind, so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind give identical sums; the expenditure side closes at 283.98 under both, and the contribution side's single row is monetary under both. Tested on this filing, not inherited.
escalation_note: (1) Schedule B row 1's amount cell was escalated to 900 dpi: it renders '38.9' plus a final digit written HEAVILY OVER another glyph (an 8 formed on top of an earlier character), unreadable as a shape. The page's own arithmetic settles it uniquely — 283.98 - 89.96 - 155.04 = 38.98 — so 38.98 is recorded and nothing was nudged. (2) Schedule A row 1's amount cell renders '283.98' with the '8' drawn twice and looped over itself; the same figure is printed twice more on the same page (subtotal and total), so the reading is corroborated inside its own document. (3) Schedule A row 1's DATE cell was escalated to 1200 dpi because the sheet's left edge is CUT OFF BY THE SCAN: the crop renders '/03/22' preceded by the right-hand strokes of a clipped leading digit consistent with a 4. Recorded verbatim as '4/03/22' at low confidence with needs_review=1 — the loss is reproduction loss (§C6), not redaction and not a filer omission, and the leading digit was NOT reconstructed from any other part of the document.

2.measure_note: A WASHED-OUT PINK/GREY PHOTOCOPY at -0.4 deg skew: the full-width scan found only 4 h_rules, so the §A2/§C6 `--col` RECOVERY was required — rowbands.py --col 78.5,92.3 returned 13 rules, of which 16.31 -> 61.33 (pitch ~4.5) are the grid rules it could still see and 84.45 / 88.15 belong to the candidate box; the rules below 61.33 are lost to the wash-out and are NOT declared here (they carry no entries). ⚠ THE FIRST ROW'S TOP RULE IS ALSO LOST, so band 1 is EXTRAPOLATED one pitch up from the first detected rule (11.81 -> 16.31) and was PROVED before use, per the §A1 first-entry control: the crop pct:77.50,11.81,14.80,4.50@p2 rendered '283.98' (the amount recorded for row 1), so the single written entry does sit on band 1 — the filer did not skip a line, and there is no banner or voided row above it. NEGATIVE CONTROL one band past the entry: pct:77.50,16.31,14.80,4.55@p2 rendered an EMPTY cell crossed only by the long vertical pen stroke the filer drew down the unused amount column — a stroke across the LEFTOVER GRID, which consumes no row and shifts no index (§E3), not a voided row. The column bands for Date/Name/Address are approximate (the wash-out defeats the vertical scan and the sheet's left edge is cut off by the scan, so the Date column is clipped); only the AMOUNT band is a proved measurement, and it is the one every row value is taken from.

3.measure_note: Schedule B on the same washed-out photocopy stock (-0.7 deg skew). The full-width scan returned 16 rules but displaced ~0.3 pct from where they fall inside the amount column, so the `--col 76,92` recovery was used and ITS rules are declared: 15.16 -> 77.09 = 15 bands (the 13.96 rule above them is the column-header underline; 80.33 / 85.25 belong to the candidate box). TWO-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi: pct:75.94,15.16,16.10,3.82@p3 rendered '38.9' + an over-written final digit (row 1, recorded 38.98 by the page's unique closure) and pct:75.94,22.77,16.10,3.91@p3 rendered '155.04' (row 3, the last written row). ONE-PAST CONTROL: pct:75.94,26.68,16.10,3.91@p3 rendered an EMPTY boxed cell, so nothing follows row 3 and no row hides below the last rule.

THE CONTRIBUTION SIDE IS THE WAVE'S `cumulative-exact` EXCEPTION and is flagged as such in recon — the one row closes on Box C and on both Schedule A footers, while the promoted per-period Box B prints an oval zero. The close box holds a heavily struck-out figure followed by a hand-drawn oval 0 and a small scrawl; it is a cover cell, transcribed by the cover tranche as 0, and it is not adjudicated here.
